transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO - ArkBridge), Marcus Lee (Infra Manager - ArkBridge), Priya Anand (Security Architect - ArkBridge)

Auto-summary (auto): Discuss hardware footprint and secure offline update process for air-gapped private deployment.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, joined by Samir, our solutions engineer. How's it going on your side?
[00:07] Dr. Elena: Hi Jordan, hi Samir. Good, thanks. We wanted to get into what a fully isolated deployment looks like for ArkBridge — low latency, strict update windows, and procurement realities.
[00:20] Marcus: Yeah and important for us is we cannot have any outbound network to pull images, so updates have to be physically transported and cryptographically verified.
[00:30] Samir: Totally — that's a common ask. We support private deployments where the control plane is customer-managed. For air-gapped flows we use signed artifacts, sha256 verification, and can provide an offline bundle you can import via sealed media.
[00:44] Priya: When you say signed artifacts, is that with your key or can we bring our own keys, like an HSM-backed signing process?
[00:51] Samir: You can absolutely use your own KMS/HSM. The recommended pattern is we produce a release image that Redwood signs; you validate the signature using the public key from our release pipeline. If you need, we can also support customer-signed images — we can accept a signed manifest that you produce.
[01:08] Dr. Elena: Ok. For compliance we'll need a key-injection process that doesn't touch internet-facing KMS. So offline key injecting into the HSM — is that supported?
[01:18] Samir: Yes, we have documented procedures for offline key import: export wrapped keys via your HSM vendor tooling, then bring into the air-gapped environment. We'll map to the same configuration in the runtime. There was a note earlier about a "cassette" workflow and I want to confirm, we mean physically transported USB or encrypted disk?
[01:33] Marcus: Encrypted SSDs we expect — USB is possible but procurement prefers sealed SSDs with tamper-evident packaging.
[01:40] Jordan: Understood. From the pricing/bandwidth angle, one of the big levers is GPU choice. Can you tell us what you're planning procurement-wise?
[01:48] Marcus: We have tentative approval for A100s but the board is considering pushing for H100s. Concern is power and cooling — racks are constrained in the new facility.
[01:58] Samir: H100s will give better throughput per GPU, but they also consume more power and require support for PCIe NVLink? There are also different performance characteristics for int8/quantized runs that can lower memory requirements.
[02:12] Dr. Elena: We're trying to map expected token/sec for our main workloads. Average sequence length is about 512 tokens for clinical summarization, with bursts up to 2k for whole-report ingest. Can you help size nodes for that?
[02:24] Samir: Yes — we'll run a bench that models 512 and 2k sequences. Preliminary thumb-rules: with FP16 or q4_int8 on an A100, you might see X tokens/sec per GPU for 7B/13B models; H100 improves latency for large seqs. I'll produce concrete numbers.
[02:40] Jordan: Also curious — is there a way to reduce physical footprint by using batching and KV-prefix caching? I know Redwood's runtime has prefix caching.
[02:50] Samir: Exactly. Caching common prefixes and continuous batching helps you increase throughput without adding GPUs. There's a trade-off between latency SLO and batching window. For ArkBridge we can suggest a config that keeps median latency under your target while using less raw GPU.
[03:05] Marcus: On maintenance, how do you handle security patches? Our security policy says quarterly patches, but for some critical fixes we might want an emergency window. How are rollbacks handled in an offline environment?
[03:16] Samir: For air-gapped deployments rollbacks are manual: we keep previous signed images in your offline repo and you can redeploy them. We recommend running canary on a staging rack before the facility-wide roll. For emergency patches we'd produce an incremental signed patch you can import — same verification process.
[03:33] Priya: We need to see audit logs for model requests and admin actions for SOC2 evidence. What format do logs come in and can they be exported from the private runtime?
[03:42] Samir: Yes, the private runtime emits structured logs with per-request metadata (model version, route, token counts, timestamps). We can produce an example log sample and an export tool that writes to your SIEM in offline mode — we support batched log export via signed bundles.
[03:58] Jordan: Quick question on SLA: if we do the Redwood Private option vs Dedicated, what uptime and support differences should ArkBridge expect?
[04:06] Samir: Dedicated is managed by us with SLA-backed availability and 24/7 support. Private (on-prem) is customer-managed infrastructure with Redwood providing support under a different tier — for air-gapped it's typically a premium enterprise plan with runbook-driven support; we can include remote runbook consults but on-site support would be a separate contract.
[04:25] Dr. Elena: Makes sense. Procurement timeline — we are aiming to sign hardware purchase orders in mid-Jan and want the software contract to align so that we can have delivery and install by March. Is that feasible?
[04:36] Jordan: Yes, that's doable. We'll align docs and an initial benchmark before you commit to H100 purchases.
[04:42] Marcus: For benchmarks, can Redwood bring a downsampled image and bench tool that we can run on a single rack to validate latency/throughput?
[04:51] Samir: We have a bench harness that runs synthetic and replay workloads. We'll provide the harness as an offline bundle you can run locally; it outputs token/sec, GPU util, power draw estimates. We'll also include a recorder so you can replay a week's worth of anonymized traffic if you want.
[05:08] Priya: About signing — we will need to validate signature chains; do you provide certificate chains or just raw signatures?
[05:15] Samir: We provide both: signed manifests along with the certificate chain and verification tooling. All artifacts are SHA-256 hashed; we can also provide an offline verification script.
[05:25] Dr. Elena: Any gotchas around kernel/driver dependencies? Our ops team is strict about distro and driver versions.
[05:32] Samir: The runtime depends on specific CUDA and driver versions. For air-gapped installs we bundle the exact driver packages and OS-level packages you need. We'll provide a preflight checklist to verify node compatibility. We also document the minimal kernel version.
[05:47] Jordan: I'm going to summarize so everyone's clear: Samir will produce a per-GPU throughput estimate for A100/H100 and three vGPU density options, provide the offline release/update checklist and signed-image process, and share the bench harness. ArkBridge will confirm their KMS/HSM constraints and rack power/cooling numbers.
[06:06] Marcus: Correct. Also, we'd appreciate a sample audit log export and a short SOC2 evidence extract.
[06:12] Samir: We'll put those in the follow-up bundle.
[06:16] Dr. Elena: One last item — are there any licensing restrictions for models you ship in air-gapped mode? Some of our compliance folks worry about model weight redistribution.
[06:25] Samir: We respect model licensing; for curated models we ship only ones cleared for redistribution or we provide an integration path to your in-house weights. We'll document per-model redistrib constraints.
[06:36] Jordan: Great. Any other questions from ArkBridge?
[06:40] Priya: How do you handle secrets rotation in an offline world? We can't rely on online CA for cert rotation.
[06:47] Samir: We support manual rotation procedures: generate new keys in your HSM, sign new manifests, and rotate at your cadence. The runtime supports hot-reload of some secrets; others require a service restart which we document.
[06:58] Marcus: About physical updates — does Redwood have an approved carrier/process for shipping update media? Our legal needs a chain-of-custody for media.
[07:08] Jordan: We can provide recommended carriers and a template chain-of-custody document. For particularly sensitive installs we also offer a third-party concierge service (at extra cost) to manage transfers.
[07:22] Dr. Elena: Thanks. This was helpful. Looking forward to the bench numbers.
[07:26] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the bundle and schedule the benchmark.
[07:30] (call continues with questions about specific rack PDU details and then closes)
